quote: Okay. I'm driving right now. But go ahead and ask. Go ahead.
stewart_read: Customer discloses a mobility/attention constraint analogous to the shopping-customer protocol. The rep does not pause to acknowledge safety or offer a callback, just proceeds with the verify script.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep should have offered a brief callback for safety/quality of qualification. Strategic read: rep judged the questions simple enough to complete verbally without needing a callback, which the transcript supports since the customer answered every item without difficulty.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to briefly acknowledge the driving disclosure ('no problem, I'll keep this quick') before diving in — costs one line, builds rapport, and protects against safety liability.

quote: It's my son. My son and myself.
stewart_read: Son is on title as a co-owner and later identified as the likely credit-qualifying party — this is a textbook adult-child-decision-maker scenario, but the rep never returns to Elliot's inclusion in any future appointment because no appointment is ever set.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep should have flagged 'let's make sure Elliot is on the call too' per protocol. Strategic read is weak here since no appointment discussion happens at all, so there's no venue to apply the protocol yet — this is a missed setup rather than a missed close.
coaching_implication: When the co-title-holder is also the credit-qualifying party, that's a compounding reason he must be on any future appointment — rep should log this explicitly for whenever booking resumes.

quote: Yeah. That's what the regular yeah. Shingles. I think it's shingles. Yeah. But I think it needs it might need to be replaced.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers a roof-replacement signal. The rep partially bridges with 'we have our own in house roofing' but stops there — never asks about timeline, never offers to route to the roofing team, never treats it as a second product opportunity.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep gave a generic acknowledgment and moved on without building the bridge into an actual routing action. Strategic read: unlikely to be deliberate, since the schema's example bridge (SESSION18_fcbf33c1) shows a full routing offer is achievable in seconds and nothing in this call suggests the rep is saving it for later.
coaching_implication: The one-line mention is a good instinct but incomplete — coach the rep to follow with 'want me to have our roofing team take a look at that too?' to fully capture the signal per the schema's positive example.

quote: Do you have a credit score or your son have a credit score over six seventy?
stewart_read: Rep runs the credit qualifier correctly at the schema-stated 670 threshold, and appropriately allows for the son's credit to qualify since he's a co-title-holder.
coaching_implication: No coaching gap here — this is the qualifier run as designed. Worth noting as a positive contrast if the rep has drifted on this number in other calls.

quote: I can take a picture when I get home and send it to you at this number right here that you're calling from?
stewart_read: Customer is engaged enough to proactively confirm the logistics of sending her bill — a moment where the rep could reinforce why the picture matters (savings, urgency) but instead just confirms the number to text.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep missed a chance to re-anchor value before ending the call. Strategic read: the call is already at its natural end and the rep may be avoiding over-selling to someone driving — but nothing indicates this was deliberate.
coaching_implication: A single reinforcing line ('great, once I get that I can show you what solar could look like for your bill') would have kept the thread alive instead of ending on pure logistics.

quote: Alright. There you go. Sounds good. Okay. Okay.
stewart_read: The call ends without any appointment being proposed, no day/time, no recap, no handshake — the entire button-up section of the script is absent.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep genuinely dropped the ball and never got to booking. Strategic read: rep may be intentionally deferring the appointment ask until the bill photo is received (a legitimate paid-lead-gating pattern) — but even so, no callback time or promise of a specific follow-up window was given, so the deferral itself is unanchored.
coaching_implication: Even when gating the appointment on bill receipt, the rep should state a concrete next step: 'once I get that photo today, I'll call you back this evening to get you on the calendar' — anchors the follow-up instead of leaving it open-ended.
